summary: John Muir was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the East India Company College, Glasgow, and Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (1828–1853), was principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1844), and held a post at the University of Edinburgh.
John Myrdhin Reynolds works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued traditional studies under teachers Lopon Tenzin Namdak, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, and Namkhai Norbu.

John Nemec is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Rochester, UC Santa Barbara, Oxford, and Penn, studying under Alexis Sanderson and Ludo Rocher. He is an Associate Professor of Indian Religions and South Asian Studies at the University of Virginia.

Philosopher John Niemeyer Findlay studied at the University of Pretoria, Balliol College, Oxford, and the University of Graz. His career included posts at Pretoria, Otago, Newcastle, King's College London, Texas at Austin, Yale, and Boston University.

Linguist John Okell studied at The Queen's College, Oxford, and trained under Hla Pe, Anna J. Allott, and Richard Keith Sprigg. From 1959 to 1999, he was a research associate at SOAS University of London.

A scholar of Buddhist and religious studies, John P. Keenan earned his PhD at Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota and studied under Noriaki Hakamaya. He was a research fellow at Nanzan University and later taught at Middlebury College.

John Peile was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cambridge and under Theodor Benfey. He spent his career at Cambridge as a Fellow and Tutor at Christ's College, Reader of Comparative Philology, and president of Newnham College.
John Pickford was an Indology scholar who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He served as a professor at the University of Madras.

Scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology John Powers studied at Holy Cross, McMaster, and Virginia. His academic appointments include posts at Virginia Commonwealth, San Francisco, Australian National University, Deakin University, and Melbourne.

John R. B. Campbell works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Columbia under Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb, while also receiving traditional instruction from the 14th Dalai Lama, Denma Lochö Rinpoche, and others.

John R. McRae worked in Buddhist studies and sinology, earning his PhD from Yale under Stanley Weinstein and studying under Seizan Yanagida. He held posts at Cornell, Indiana University Bloomington, Komazawa University, and Soka University.
John Riley Perks is a Buddhist studies scholar. He received traditional training under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

John Ronald Newman works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He received his PhD from Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, studied under Geshe Lobsang Wangdrak, and served as Assistant Professor of Asian Religions at New College of Florida.

John Ross Carter was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at King's College London, SOAS, and Harvard under Wilfred Cantwell Smith. He served as a professor at Colgate University from around 1972 to 2012.

John S. Strong is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from Chicago under Frank E. Reynolds. He spent his career primarily at Bates College, alongside visiting appointments at Chicago, Harvard, Princeton, and Stanford.

Linguist and Indologist John Shakespear studied under John Richardson. He held professorships of oriental languages at the Royal Military College, Sandhurst (1805–1809) and Addiscombe Military Seminary (1809–1829).
John Shore was an Indology and history scholar who served as President of The Asiatic Society, succeeding William Jones.

John Stratton Hawley is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Amherst and under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He taught at Bowdoin College before becoming a professor at Columbia University around 1986.
Philosopher John Stuart Mill studied at University College London from around 1828 to 1830. He held a post at the East India Company from approximately 1823 to 1858.

Historian John Sydenham Furnivall studied at Cambridge (Trinity Hall and Trinity College) and Leiden University. He founded the Burma Research Society in 1910 and held a post at the University of Cambridge from around 1936 to 1941.
